Saudi Arabia, Pakistan and Turkey have signed a defence pact, saying an attack on one of them would be seen as an attack on all three. Some analysts have described this deal between majority-Muslim powers as the "Islamic Nato" - though the members have not used that term. 

So do the signatories of the Mecca Joint Defence Agreement really intend to come to their partners' rescue - particularly if it risks joining a wider conflict in the Middle East? 

Iran has launched strikes on Saudi Arabia and other Gulf countries throughout the war with the US and Israel. In recent days, Iran-backed Houthis in Yemen have targetted a Saudi tanker and oil refinery. 

At the same time, Pakistan has been trying to broker peace between Iranian leaders and the administration of President Donald Trump. And Pakistan's rival, India, has built its own relationships with Israel and the United Arab Emirates.

videos.title: We investigated the reality for people working on zero-hour contracts
videos.description:
The number of people on zero-hours contracts in the UK has risen to a record high, despite plans to crackdown on their use, according to a report shared exclusively with ITV News.

There are currently 1.24 million people employed on zero-hours arrangements, up by 207,000 since Labour took power in July 2024 with a pledge to ban "exploitative" contracts.

Under a zero-hours contract, workers have no guarantee of any shifts and are only called upon when they're needed - often with very little notice - meaning many have no idea how much they will earn from month to month.

Shifts can be cancelled at the last minute and workers are not entitled to any compensation, despite often already paying for transport and childcare.

Labour had initially pledged - before their 2024 manifesto - to protect workers by banning zero-hours contracts entirely, before watering this down to only outlaw "exploitative" zero-hours contracts.

Businesses, and some workers, say zero-hours contracts are beneficial because they allow flexibility, and the hospitality industry has warned that a crackdown could devastate the sector.
